[EFFECT]
Wind speed has a mostly negative effect on predicted bike demand that becomes increasingly pronounced as wind picks up. At very low wind speeds (roughly 0–8 km/h), the model's contribution is close to zero — essentially neutral. Once wind speeds climb above about 17 km/h (normalised ≈ 0.25), the contribution drops steeply and continuously, reaching its lowest point at the highest recorded speeds (~55 km/h), where it suppresses predicted demand by about −0.34 in log space — a meaningful downward multiplier. In short, calm conditions barely affect demand, but strong winds push predicted rentals noticeably lower.

[IMPORTANCE]
Windspeed ranks **8th out of 9 features** in overall importance (importance score: 0.014), making it one of the weakest drivers in the model. It is far less influential than the hour of day (rank 1), temperature (rank 2), year (rank 3), or humidity (rank 5), and only slightly more impactful than the holiday flag (rank 9).

[RECOMMENDATION]
On days when strong winds are forecast (above roughly 17 km/h), you can modestly scale back bike rebalancing efforts and staffing, as demand is expected to soften — but since wind is a minor factor overall, operational decisions should be primarily driven by the time of day and temperature forecasts.
